D: Young Australian light horsemen ride into the famous charge at Beersheba during the First World War.
P: Serve the billy tea when the line forms up for the charge.
S: Trooper's bully beef rissoles with tomato relish
Bully beef from the ration tin mashed with onion, fried in rissoles, tomato relish.

Corned beef rissoles with potato, onion and parsley, fried crisp and served with tomato relish. Boil 500g peeled potatoes until tender and mash. Mix with 340g tinned corned beef, 1 grated onion, a handful of chopped parsley, 1 egg and plenty of pepper. Shape into 12 small rissoles, roll in 60g dried breadcrumbs and fry in 3 tbsp oil for 4 minutes a side until crisp. Serve hot with 150g tomato relish.
Labneh swirled with olive oil and za'atar, olives and warm pita.
Spoon 500g labneh into a shallow dish, swirl with 3 tbsp olive oil and scatter over 2 tbsp za'atar. Serve with 200g mixed olives and 6 warm pita breads.
M: Meinertzhagen's decoy beef and stout stew
Chuck beef, carrot and onion slow-cooked in stout.

Chuck steak slow-braised with stout, onion, carrot and thyme until falling apart, with buttery mash to soak up the gravy. Toss 1kg diced chuck in 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches in oil. Add 2 diced onions, 3 carrots and 2 garlic cloves and cook 5 minutes. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 375ml stout, 500ml beef stock, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Spoon the stew over the mash.
Dave Mitchell's Beersheba lamb and date pilaf
Lamb, rice and dates, for Dave, the new recruit.

Lamb shoulder simmered with cumin, cinnamon and onion, then cooked through rice with dates, finished with toasted almonds and parsley. Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot, add the onion and cook until soft. Add the cumin, cinnamon and 500ml stock and simmer covered until the lamb is tender. Stir in the rice, dates and the rest of the stock, cover and cook on low until the rice is done. Toast the almonds and scatter over with chopped parsley.
W: Syrupy orange and semolina cake, served warm. Jaffa oranges from the Palestine front.

Heat the oven to 180C. Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, then beat in 3 eggs, the zest of 2 oranges, 150g fine semolina, 100g almond meal, 75g self-raising flour and 125ml orange juice. Bake in a lined 22cm tin for 40 minutes. Boil another 125ml orange juice with 100g sugar for 5 minutes and pour over the hot cake.
Chewy oat, coconut and golden syrup biscuits.

Golden oat and coconut biscuits made with golden syrup, crisp at the edges and chewy in the centre, the Australian remembrance biscuit. Mix 100g rolled oats, 150g plain flour, 80g desiccated coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stir in 1 tsp bicarb dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water so it foams. Pour into the dry mix and stir well. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays, leaving room to spread, and bake at 170C for 12 to 14 minutes until golden. Cool on the trays to crisp up.
K: Strong black tea sweetened with condensed milk.

Strong black tea stewed in a billy and sweetened with condensed milk the way the troops drank it, rich and caramel sweet. Bring 1.2L water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Add 6 black tea bags, take off the heat and steep 5 minutes for a strong brew. Remove the bags. Spoon 1 to 2 tbsp condensed milk into each of 4 enamel mugs, pour over the hot tea and stir until creamy.
